questions.text: Under Ind AS 115, which of the following is NOT one of the 5 steps in the revenue recognition model?
questions.optionA: Identify the contract(s) with a customer
questions.optionC: Estimate the fair value of non-monetary assets surrendered
questions.optionD: Allocate transaction price to performance obligations
questions.explanation: The 5 steps under Ind AS 115 are: (1) Identify contract with customer, (2) Identify performance obligations, (3) Determine transaction price, (4) Allocate transaction price, and (5) Recognize revenue. Estimating fair value of surrendered assets is an Ind AS 16 / Ind AS 38 concept, not part of Ind AS 115.

questions.text: A contract modification is accounted for as a separate contract under Ind AS 115 if:
questions.optionA: The scope increases because of distinct goods/services and the price reflects standalone selling prices.
questions.optionB: The customer requests a 10% discount on the remaining goods.
questions.optionC: The remaining goods are not distinct from goods transferred prior to modification.
questions.optionD: The entity chooses to treat it as a cumulative catch-up adjustment.
questions.explanation: According to paragraph 20 of Ind AS 115, a contract modification is treated as a separate contract if the scope increases due to addition of promised goods/services that are distinct AND the price increases by an amount reflecting standalone selling prices.

questions.text: Under Ind AS 115, variable consideration is included in transaction price only to the extent that:
questions.optionA: Management expects an audit sign-off by the statutory auditor.
questions.optionB: It is highly probable that a significant reversal in cumulative revenue will not occur when uncertainty is resolved.
questions.optionC: The customer signs a formal bank guarantee for the bonus amount.
questions.optionD: The variable amount exceeds 25% of the fixed contract value.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 56 of Ind AS 115 outlines the constraint on variable consideration: it is included only if it is highly probable that a significant reversal in the amount of cumulative revenue recognized will not occur once uncertainty is resolved.

questions.text: Which indicator suggests that performance obligation is satisfied over time rather than at a point in time?
questions.optionA: The customer has physical possession of the asset.
questions.optionB: The customer has legal title to the asset.
questions.optionC: The entity’s performance does not create an asset with alternative use and entity has an enforceable right to payment for performance completed to date.
questions.optionD: The customer has accepted the goods after factory trial run.
questions.explanation: Ind AS 115 Paragraph 35(c) states that an entity transfers control over time if the performance does not create an asset with an alternative use to the entity AND the entity has an enforceable right to payment for performance completed to date.

questions.text: Incremental costs of obtaining a contract with a customer are capitalized under Ind AS 115 if:
questions.optionA: The costs are incurred regardless of whether the contract is obtained.
questions.optionB: The entity expects to recover those costs.
questions.optionC: The amortization period is 6 months or less and entity expenses them immediately.
questions.optionD: The costs consist of general administrative overheads.
questions.explanation: Ind AS 115 Paragraph 91 requires entities to recognize as an asset the incremental costs of obtaining a contract if the entity expects to recover them (e.g. sales commission paid only upon winning the contract).

questions.text: What is the minimum notice period required for calling a meeting of the Board of Directors under Section 173(3) of the Companies Act 2013?
questions.explanation: Section 173(3) requires not less than 7 days notice in writing to every director at his address registered with the company.

questions.text: What is the required statutory quorum for a Board meeting of a public company under Section 174(1)?
questions.optionA: 1/3rd of total strength or 2 directors, whichever is higher.
questions.optionB: 1/4th of total strength or 3 directors, whichever is lower.
questions.optionD: Half of total strength including the Chairman.
questions.explanation: Section 174(1) provides that the quorum for a Board meeting shall be 1/3rd of its total strength or two directors, whichever is higher.

questions.text: Which matter CANNOT be approved through a circular resolution passed under Section 175?
questions.optionA: Noting the declaration of independence by independent directors
questions.optionB: Approval of annual financial statements and Board’s report
questions.optionC: Allotment of shares within authorized capital
questions.optionD: Opening of a new bank current account
questions.explanation: Under Section 179(3) read with Rule 8 of Companies Rules, approval of annual financial statements and Board report MUST be passed at a physical/video Board meeting and cannot be passed by circular resolution.

questions.text: Under Section 173(1), what is the maximum permissible gap between two consecutive Board meetings?
questions.explanation: Section 173(1) mandates at least four Board meetings every year with not more than 120 days intervening between two consecutive meetings.

questions.text: In a company where the total strength of the Board is 9 directors, and 7 directors are interested in a contract, what is the valid quorum under Section 174(3)?
questions.optionA: No meeting can be held; must refer to General Meeting.
questions.optionB: 2 disinterested directors present at the meeting.
questions.optionC: The interested directors can vote with prior ROC permission.
questions.optionD: Quorum must be at least 3 directors.
questions.explanation: Under Section 174(3), where the number of interested directors exceeds or is equal to 2/3rds of total strength, the remaining non-interested directors present (not being less than 2) shall constitute the quorum.

questions.text: When the percentage change in quantity demanded is less than the percentage change in price, the demand is said to be:
questions.explanation: When elasticity of demand Ep < 1, percentage change in quantity demanded is less than percentage change in price, indicating relatively inelastic demand.

questions.text: If two goods are complementary goods (e.g. pen and ink), the cross elasticity of demand between them will be:
questions.explanation: Complementary goods have a negative cross price elasticity because an increase in the price of one leads to a decrease in the demand for the other.

questions.text: The point of satiety in consumer utility theory occurs when:
questions.optionD: Average utility is equal to price
questions.explanation: The point of satiety is the state where total utility reaches its maximum and marginal utility becomes zero.

questions.text: An indifference curve is convex to the origin because of:
questions.explanation: The convexity of an indifference curve reflects the diminishing marginal rate of substitution between two commodities.

questions.text: When preparing a Bank Reconciliation Statement starting with Debit Balance as per Cash Book, cheques issued but not presented for payment should be:
questions.explanation: Cheques issued were deducted from Cash Book but bank has not yet debited them, so the Pass Book balance is higher. Hence, we add back.

questions.text: A debit balance in the customer’s account in the Bank Pass Book indicates:
questions.explanation: From the bank’s perspective, a debit balance indicates the customer owes money to the bank, which signifies a Bank Overdraft.

questions.text: Direct collection of interest and dividends by the bank on behalf of the customer causes:
questions.optionA: Pass Book balance to be higher than Cash Book balance
questions.optionB: Cash Book balance to be higher than Pass Book balance
questions.explanation: Direct collection is credited in the Pass Book immediately, making Pass Book balance higher until recorded in the Cash Book.

questions.text: Under the Diminishing Balance Method, depreciation is calculated on the:
questions.optionB: Written Down Value (WDV) at beginning of year
questions.explanation: Under WDV or diminishing balance method, depreciation is computed on the reducing book value at the beginning of each financial year.

questions.text: In the absence of an explicit Partnership Agreement, what rate of interest is allowed on advances/loans given by a partner to the firm?
questions.explanation: Under Section 13(d) of the Indian Partnership Act 1932, a partner is entitled to interest at 6% p.a. on any loan or advance given beyond capital.

questions.text: The Sacrificing Ratio of existing partners at the time of admission of a new partner is defined as:
questions.optionA: New Profit Ratio - Old Profit Ratio
questions.optionB: Old Profit Ratio - New Profit Ratio
questions.optionD: Old Ratio multiplied by New Ratio
questions.explanation: Sacrificing Ratio = Old Profit Sharing Ratio - New Profit Sharing Ratio.

questions.text: Super Profit under goodwill valuation is calculated as:
questions.optionC: Weighted Profit divided by Normal Rate
questions.optionD: Net Profit before tax minus dividends
questions.explanation: Super Profit = Actual/Average Maintainable Profit - Normal Profit.

questions.text: Profit or loss arising on the revaluation of assets and liabilities upon admission of a partner is credited or debited to:
questions.optionA: All partners including new partner in new ratio
questions.optionB: Old partners’ capital accounts in old profit sharing ratio
questions.optionC: Sacrificing partners only in sacrificing ratio
questions.explanation: Revaluation profit/loss pertains to the period prior to the admission of the new partner, hence belongs strictly to old partners in their old ratio.

questions.text: Under the Sale of Goods Act 1930, a Condition is a stipulation:
questions.optionA: Collateral to the main purpose of the contract
questions.optionB: Essential to the main purpose of the contract
questions.optionD: Governed solely by customs of trade
questions.explanation: Section 12(2) defines a Condition as a stipulation essential to the main purpose of the contract, breach of which gives rise to a right to treat the contract as repudiated.

questions.text: The Latin maxim "Caveat Emptor" under commercial law implies:
questions.explanation: Caveat Emptor signifies "Let the buyer beware"—the buyer must satisfy himself about the quality and fitness of goods before purchase.

questions.text: An unpaid seller of goods can exercise his Right of Lien when:
questions.optionA: The goods are sold on credit and credit term has not expired
questions.optionB: He is in possession of the goods as agent or bailee for buyer
questions.optionC: The buyer has obtained lawful possession of the goods
questions.optionD: The goods have been handed over to a common carrier without reservation
questions.explanation: Under Section 47, an unpaid seller can retain possession of goods (Right of Lien) until payment if the goods are still in his actual possession.

questions.text: Which characteristic of an incorporated company ensures that the death or insolvency of members does NOT affect its existence?
questions.explanation: Perpetual succession means members may come and go, but the company continues in existence until dissolved by law.

questions.text: In the Law of Variable Proportions, Stage II (Stage of Diminishing Returns) ends where:
questions.optionA: Marginal product equals zero and total product is maximum
questions.optionC: Marginal product is equal to average product
questions.optionD: Total product begins to rise steeply
questions.explanation: Stage II concludes where MP = 0, at which point Total Product reaches its absolute maximum.

questions.text: The mathematical shape of the Average Fixed Cost (AFC) curve is a:
questions.explanation: Since TFC = AFC × Q remains constant, the AFC curve forms a rectangular hyperbola asymptotic to both axes.

questions.text: When Marginal Cost (MC) is less than Average Cost (AC), the Average Cost curve is:
questions.explanation: Whenever MC is below AC, it pulls AC downwards; hence Average Cost is falling.

questions.text: Returns to Scale is a concept applicable strictly to the:
questions.explanation: Returns to scale examines how output responds when ALL input factors are varied simultaneously in the long run.

questions.text: Under Perfect Competition, the demand curve faced by an individual firm is:
questions.explanation: In pure competition, the firm is a price taker, facing a perfectly horizontal demand curve where P = AR = MR.

questions.text: Paul Sweezy’s Kinked Demand Curve model is formulated to explain:
questions.explanation: The kinked demand curve explains why oligopoly firms maintain rigid prices despite cost variations.

questions.text: In the phases of a Business Cycle, the highest point of economic expansion is designated as:
questions.explanation: The Peak or Boom represents the turning point where economic activity reaches maximum capacity before contraction begins.

questions.text: Under Monopoly market structure, Marginal Revenue (MR) is always:
questions.explanation: To sell an additional unit, a monopolist must lower the price of all units, meaning MR lies below AR (price).

questions.text: If a : b = 2 : 3 and b : c = 4 : 5, then the compound ratio a : b : c is equal to:
questions.explanation: Multiply a:b by 4 to get 8:12, and b:c by 3 to get 12:15. Thus, a : b : c = 8 : 12 : 15.

questions.text: What is the numerical value of log₂(32)?
questions.explanation: Since 32 = 2⁵, log₂(2⁵) = 5 × log₂(2) = 5 × 1 = 5.

questions.text: The sub-duplicate ratio of 49 : 81 is:
questions.explanation: Sub-duplicate ratio of a : b is √a : √b. Hence, √49 : √81 = 7 : 9.

questions.text: If x = (25)^(1/2) × (8)^(1/3), the value of x is:
questions.explanation: √25 = 5 and ∛8 = 2. Therefore, 5 × 2 = 10.

questions.text: What is the effective annual rate of interest corresponding to a nominal rate of 6% per annum compounded semi-annually?
The difference between simple interest and compound interest on ₹ 10,000 for 2 years at 10% per annum is:
An annuity in which cash payments are made at the END of each period is known as:
questions.explanation: An annuity where payments occur at the end of each payment period is defined as an Ordinary Annuity or Immediate Annuity.

questions.text: A sinking fund is primarily established by an organization for:
questions.optionB: Accumulating funds to redeem a long-term liability or replace an asset
questions.optionC: Paying interim quarterly dividends to shareholders
questions.explanation: A sinking fund is created by periodically setting aside amounts to accumulate a specific capital sum needed to pay off a bond or replace machinery.

questions.explanation: Only the person to whom the offer is made can accept it.

questions.text: Which flowchart diagram correctly represents the contract formation process?
questions.explanation: Proposal accepted becomes agreement, and enforceable agreement becomes contract.
